agyos_skill.instructions: Connect module-level working rules to existing domain language, contracts, and decisions. This is an orchestration skill, not a second DDD methodology or an automatic documentation generator. - The user asks to implement a new business module, without needing to name this skill. - The user asks to document an existing module or maintain a confirmed responsibility change. - An authorized module change needs local instructions and canonical knowledge pointers. Do not start setup for an ordinary bug, styling change, internal refactor with unchanged boundaries, or a new directory/UI component that simply inherits parent conventions. For design discussion or an audit alone, inspect and report without creating files. Intent-based selection is not a background hook and does not grant permission for unrelated code, commits, pushes, or business choices. Read applicable project and ancestor harness instructions, the existing map, requirements, relevant code, and contracts. Identify the module's responsibilities, non-responsibilities, state ownership, and actual consumers. Directory names alone do not establish a bounded context. Surface material ambiguities instead of inventing business rules. For an existing boundary change, use `change-impact` first. Its read-only and authorization constraints still apply; do not run an unrelated development workflow. The project-level instruction source owns global constraints, module navigation, and cross-module collaboration. A local `AGENTS.md` owns only additional module constraints: responsibilities, state ownership, public-interface pointers, and verification entry points. Local rules cannot waive project-wide constraints. Reuse an established `CLAUDE.md` or other active harness surface instead of forcing a rename or maintaining two copies. If parent instructions already cover the module and no local rule is missing, link that source and do not create
